summary: The submission-time de-duplication (resource_governor.submit(), lock-protected via superboss-register.py's _write_lock()) correctly fixes the literal reported incident (a single trigger re-firing every 60s for the same task_identity). However, dispatch_one() in scripts/resource_governor.py selects the next queued row via next_queued_task() BEFORE acquiring dispatch_core.acquire_dispatch_lock(), and never re-verifies the row's status once inside that lock before calling _perform_spawn(row) -- this is precisely the TOCTOU pattern dispatch_core.has_free_slot()'s own docstring warns callers never to reintroduce. Since the design doc itself states resource_governor.py --tick is meant to be invoked by 'a governor timer or any tick script' (i.e. multiple independent trigger scripts), concurrent tick invocations are an expected real usage pattern, not a hypothetical edge case. I reproduced this live: two concurrent dispatch_one() calls against the same fixture DB both selected and dispatched the same umr_id, firing the real systemctl restart mock twice for the same unit -- the exact duplicate-dispatch failure mode this entire feature was built to make 'structurally impossible.' Architecture, schema design, metric sampling, stuck-task SIGTERM/SIGKILL protocol, and the emergency cascade are otherwise sound and well-tested (15 new tests, all passing), but this race undermines the core correctness guarantee for the governor's own dispatch loop and should be fixed (e.g. re-select-and-claim the row atomically inside acquire_dispatch_lock(), or re-check row status under the lock before spawning) before merge.
issues: Race condition in scripts/resource_governor.py dispatch_one(): next_queued_task() reads the queued row outside dispatch_core.acquire_dispatch_lock(), and the row's status is never re-verified after the lock is acquired and before _perform_spawn(row) runs. Two concurrent dispatch_one() invocations (realistic given the documented multi-trigger --tick usage) can both dispatch the same umr_id, causing a real duplicate systemctl action or duplicate veridian-task.py create -- reproduced empirically with a two-thread race against the test fixture (both calls returned action='dispatched' for the same umr_id, real spawn command fired twice). No existing test in tests/test_resource_governor.py covers concurrent dispatch_one()/run_tick() invocations, so this gap shipped untested despite being the exact failure class the feature targets.
No .github/workflows/** files are touched by this diff, so the hard rule against worker changes to workflow files does not apply here.
